title: B.C. teen rescued from 'Widowmaker' mountain trail says AI isn't to blame

reading.body:
This is a case of a language model producing route guidance that was treated as navigational fact. The system was used outside the conditions it was built for: a general conversational assistant asked to plan a real backcountry route, where the cost of a wrong answer is physical. The failure surfaced at the point of use, on the mountain, not at any review step, because the hiker acted on the output directly.

Catching this would have required a check the deployment did not have. Either the model would need to refuse or flag route-planning requests as outside its competence, or the user would need to verify the route against a map, a guidebook or a person with training before setting out. Neither happened, and the error only became visible when the described route led to terrain requiring ropes and gear the hiker did not carry.

What is not established is whether the model stated the route confidently as fact or hedged, and whether any warning it gave was seen and disregarded. The reporting records a rescue and a search manager's assessment, not a finding about the system's output or its design.

reports.title: A teen tried to navigate Canadian mountains with Claude. His trek ended in an emergency rescue
Solo teen hiker hoisted from mountain cliff after using AI to plan route, North Shore Rescue says
Teenager rescued from B.C.’s ‘Widowmaker’ after getting stranded using AI instructions
Hiker, 16, Is Rescued From ‘Widowmaker’ Ledge After Using Chatbot to Plan Route
B.C. teen rescued from 'Widowmaker' mountain trail says AI isn't to blame

summary:
A 16-year-old named Bryce Vincent Gowryluk had to be rescued in British Columbia after using the AI chatbot Claude to plan a hike. He took a gondola up Grouse Mountain and asked Claude for a route to Crown Mountain and back. The directions led him off course to the Widowmaker Arete, a 1,700ft climb that requires ropes and other gear he did not have. He became stuck at the base of a cliff, called his mother and then emergency services.

North Shore Rescue sent a helicopter, but it could not get close enough to the rock face, so two team members were hoisted down to lift him out. He was flown to a rescue base near the Cleveland Dam. Search manager Paul Markey said Gowryluk was far off his intended route and warned that AI cannot replace proper training, map and compass skills, and good decision making.
